title: From naive to native form: Shared kinematic signatures of conventionalization and acquisition in manual language
text:
This website documents data processing pipeline developed for the study From naive to native form: Shared kinematic signatures of conventionalization and acquisition in manual language. The study resulted from a short-term collaboration between two projects: On the FLExibility and Stability of Gesture-speecH Coordination (FLESH) and The Gesture-to-Sign Trajectory: Phonological Parameters in Production and Real-Time Comprehension. The pipeline covers every step from raw data processing to feature extraction and analysis.
The repository associated with this project can be found on Github.

title: From naive to native form: Shared kinematic signatures of conventionalization and acquisition in manual language
text:
Pipeline Overview
This study builds on multistep pipeline that serves to:

prepare videos for processing (A)
perform motion tracking (B)
process resulting time series (C)
extract relevant features (D)
analyze with regards to research questions (E)

Section F presents supplementary results. Note that in this workflow, each step builds on the previous one. However, it is possible to use parts of the workflow for different purposes. Section F presents extended version of results.






Note



We only store and share only already pre-processed .csv files. They are available in the Github repository. If you are interested in the raw data, contact Door Spruijt.

title: Using PCA to identify kinematic dimensions
text:
In this script, we will perform Principal Component Analysis to reduce to multidimensional matrix to orthogonal kinematic dimensions. We will then model each dimension (Principal Component) as a function of group membership (gesturer, learner, signer).
We use workflow described by Wilson Black and colleagues (2023) because it provides several sanity checks that ensure that we are not interpreting noise resulting from the sampling procedure.

Before PCA, we want to clean the dataframe such that it only contains numerical values, but so that we can still return to the group and concept identification (for visual purposes)


Custom functions
# Function to clean the data
def clean_df(df):

    # Fill NaNs with 0
    df = df.fillna(0)   # FLAGGED: this we might change, maybe not the best method (alternative: MICE)

    # Save values from groupID
    groupID = df['groupID']
    concepts = df['concept']

    # Leave only numerical cols, except groupID
    df = df.select_dtypes(include=['float64','int64'])

    # Add back correction_info
    df['groupID'] = groupID
    df['concept'] = concepts
    
    return df

title: Using PCA to identify kinematic dimensions
text:
Testing approprietness of PCA
To test whether PCA is appropriate method we will permute the data frame thousand times and see what is the correlation structure in these permuted df relative to our df. If the structure in our df varies systematically, the number of correlations should be much higher than in the permuted data

# keep only numerical columns for correlation analysis
numerical_cols = df_clean.select_dtypes(include=['float64', 'int64']).columns
df_numerical = df_clean[numerical_cols]

# Compute raw correlations
X_raw = df_numerical #.iloc[:, :-1].values  # unscaled features

obs_rs = []
obs_pvals = []

for i in range(X_raw.shape[1]):
    for j in range(i+1, X_raw.shape[1]):
        r, p = pearsonr(X_raw.iloc[:, i], X_raw.iloc[:, j])
        obs_rs.append(r)
        obs_pvals.append(p)

obs_rs = np.array(obs_rs)
obs_pvals = np.array(obs_pvals)

# Compute permutation
null_sig_counts = []
null_rs_all = []

for _ in range(1000):
    X_perm = np.apply_along_axis(np.random.permutation, 0, X_raw)

    perm_rs = []
    perm_pvals = []

    for i in range(X_raw.shape[1]):
        for j in range(i+1, X_raw.shape[1]):
            r, p = pearsonr(X_perm[:, i], X_perm[:, j])
            perm_rs.append(r)
            perm_pvals.append(p)

    perm_rs = np.array(perm_rs)
    perm_pvals = np.array(perm_pvals)

    null_sig_counts.append(np.sum(perm_pvals < 0.05))
    null_rs_all.append(np.abs(perm_rs))

null_sig_counts = np.array(null_sig_counts)
null_rs_all = np.array(null_rs_all).ravel()

This is a plot of permuted vs raw data:


Display code
alpha = 0.05 # like p < 0.05
obs_sig_count = np.sum(obs_pvals < alpha)
obs_abs_rs = np.abs(obs_rs)


plt.figure(figsize=(14, 5))

# Panel A: Count of significant correlations
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
sns.violinplot(y=null_sig_counts, color="#00BFC4")
plt.scatter([0], [obs_sig_count], color="#F8766D", s=80, zorder=5)
plt.ylabel("Count of significant correlations")
plt.title("A")

# Panel B: Magnitude of correlations
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
sns.kdeplot(null_rs_all, color="#00BFC4", linewidth=2, label="Null")
sns.kdeplot(obs_abs_rs, color="#F8766D", linewidth=2, label="Data")
plt.xlabel("Magnitude of Pearson's r")
plt.ylabel("Density")
plt.legend()
plt.title("B")

plt.suptitle("Permutation Test on Correlation Structure (1000 iterations)", fontsize=16)
plt.tight_layout()

# save the plot
plt.savefig(os.path.join(curfolder, "Plots", "permutation_test_correlations.png"), dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()









These are the detailed results of the permutation test:


Display code
X_raw = df_numerical
feature_names = df_numerical.columns.to_list()

obs_corrs = []

for i in range(X_raw.shape[1]):
    for j in range(i+1, X_raw.shape[1]):
        r, p = pearsonr(X_raw.iloc[:, i], X_raw.iloc[:, j])
        obs_corrs.append({
            "feat1": feature_names[i],
            "feat2": feature_names[j],
            "r": r,
            "abs_r": abs(r),
            "p": p
        })

obs_corrs_df = pd.DataFrame(obs_corrs)

alpha = 0.05

obs_sig_count = np.sum(obs_corrs_df["p"] < alpha)

print("Correlation test results.")
print(f"Count of significant pairwise correlations in original data at alpha = {alpha}: {obs_sig_count}")
print(f"Mean significant pairwise correlations in permuted data (n = 1000) at alpha = {alpha}: {null_sig_counts.mean():.3f}")
print(f"Min = {null_sig_counts.min()}, Max = {null_sig_counts.max()}.")

top_n = 5

top_corrs = obs_corrs_df.sort_values("abs_r", ascending=False).head(top_n)

print("\nTop 5 pairwise correlations in original data:")
for _, row in top_corrs.iterrows():
    print(f"{row['feat1']}, {row['feat2']}: {row['r']:.2f}")

Mean significant pairwise correlations in permuted data (n = 1000) at alpha = 0.05: 53.730

title: Using PCA to identify kinematic dimensions
text:
PCA all groups (fine + gross)
 Now, we first standardize the data and apply PCA to extract principal components. To inspect the results visually, we create biplots which visualize relationship between two selected principal components. Data points are color-coded on the target variable (groupID) and red arrows represent the contributions of selected variables to the PC.


See plotting functions
def interactive_PCA_biplot(score, coeff, labels=None, y=None, selected_vars=None, 
                            arrow_strength=None, pc_x=1, pc_y=2, show_labels=True,
                            concepts=None, highlight_concepts=None, le=None):
    ix, iy = pc_x - 1, pc_y - 1
    xs = score[:, ix]
    ys = score[:, iy]
    concepts = np.array(concepts) if concepts is not None else None

    if concepts is not None and len(concepts) != len(xs):
        print(f"Warning: concepts length ({len(concepts)}) doesn't match score rows ({len(xs)}). Ignoring concepts.")
        concepts = None

    def group_name(g):
        return le.inverse_transform([g])[0] if le is not None else f"Group {g}"

    # Discrete color mapping per group 
    groups = np.unique(y)
    palette = [
        '#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#2ca02c', '#d62728',

        ))

    # Highlighted concept overlays
    if concepts is not None and highlight_concepts is not None:
        for concept in highlight_concepts:
            mask = np.where(concepts == concept)[0]

            seen_groups = {}
            for idx in mask:
                group = y[idx]
                if group not in seen_groups:

                name=concept,
                text=[f"{concept} — {group_name(y[i])}" for i in representative_indices],
                hoverinfo='text',
                showlegend=True
            ))

    vars_to_plot = selected_vars if selected_vars is not None else range(coeff.shape[0])
    base_scale = 10

    for i in vars_to_plot:
        var_name = f"Var{i+1}" if labels is None else labels[i]
        scale = base_scale * (arrow_strength.get(var_name, 1.0) if arrow_strength else 1.0)

        traces.append(go.Scatter(
            x=[0, coeff[i, ix] * scale],
            y=[0, coeff[i, iy] * scale],
            mode='lines+markers+text' if show_labels else 'lines+markers',
            line=dict(color='black'),
            marker=dict(size=4),
            text=[None, var_name] if show_labels else None,
            textposition='top center',
            hovertext=var_name,
            hoverinfo='text',

        title=f"Interactive PCA Biplot — PC{pc_x} vs PC{pc_y}",
        xaxis=dict(title=f'PC{pc_x}'),
        yaxis=dict(title=f'PC{pc_y}'),
        width=900, height=700,
        hovermode='closest',
    )

    go.Figure(data=traces, layout=layout).show()

def static_PCA_biplot(score, coeff, labels=None, y=None, selected_vars=None,
                      arrow_strength=None, pc_x=1, pc_y=2, show_labels=True,
                      concepts=None, highlight_concepts=None, le=None,
                      figsize=(12, 9), save_path=None, dpi=300):
    """
    Presentation-quality static PCA biplot with centroids.

    Parameters
    ----------
    score           : np.ndarray, shape (n_samples, n_components)
    coeff           : np.ndarray, shape (n_vars, n_components)
    labels          : list of str, variable names for arrows
    y               : np.ndarray, group labels (int or str)
    selected_vars   : list of int, indices of variables to draw arrows for
    arrow_strength  : dict {var_name: scale_factor}
    pc_x, pc_y      : int, which PCs to plot (1-indexed)
    show_labels     : bool, annotate arrow tips with variable names
    concepts        : np.ndarray, concept label per sample
    highlight_concepts : list of str, concepts to highlight with star markers
    le              : sklearn LabelEncoder for decoding group labels
    figsize         : tuple
    save_path       : str or None — if given, saves figure to this path
    dpi             : int, resolution for saved figure
    """

    ix, iy = pc_x - 1, pc_y - 1
    xs = score[:, ix]
    ys = score[:, iy]
    concepts = np.array(concepts) if concepts is not None else None

    if concepts is not None and len(concepts) != len(xs):
        print(f"Warning: concepts length ({len(concepts)}) doesn't match score rows ({len(xs)}). Ignoring.")
        concepts = None

    def group_name(g):
        return le.inverse_transform([g])[0] if le is not None else f"Group {g}"

    # Palette 
    PALETTE = [
        "#878787", "#77AB00", "#00BCC2", "#8B3FAB",
        "#8172B3", "#937860", "#DA8BC3", "#8C8C8C",
    ]
    groups = np.unique(y)
    color_map = {g: PALETTE[i % len(PALETTE)] for i, g in enumerate(groups)}

    # Figure setup
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize, facecolor="#FAFAFA")
    ax.set_facecolor("#FAFAFA")

    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_linewidth(0.8)
        spine.set_color("#CCCCCC")

    ax.axhline(0, color="#CCCCCC", linewidth=0.8, zorder=0)
    ax.axvline(0, color="#CCCCCC", linewidth=0.8, zorder=0)
    ax.grid(True, linestyle="--", linewidth=0.5, color="#E0E0E0", zorder=0)

    # Scatter per group
    for g in groups:
        mask = y == g
        c = color_map[g]
        ax.scatter(
            xs[mask], ys[mask],
            color=to_rgba(c, 0.55),
            edgecolors=to_rgba(c, 0.85),
            linewidths=0.5,
            s=85,
            zorder=2,
            label=group_name(g),
        )

    # Centroids
    for g in groups:
        mask = y == g
        cx, cy = xs[mask].mean(), ys[mask].mean()
        c = color_map[g]
        ax.scatter(
            cx, cy,
            color=c,
            edgecolors="white",
            linewidths=1.8,
            s=200,
            marker="X",
            zorder=5,
        )
        ax.annotate(
            group_name(g),
            xy=(cx, cy),
            xytext=(6, 6),
            textcoords="offset points",
            fontsize=9,
            fontweight="bold",
            color=c,
            zorder=6,
        )

    # Highlighted concepts
    if concepts is not None and highlight_concepts is not None:
        for concept in highlight_concepts:
            idx_all = np.where(concepts == concept)[0]
            seen_groups = {}
            for idx in idx_all:
                g = y[idx]
                if g not in seen_groups:
                    seen_groups[g] = idx
            rep_indices = list(seen_groups.values())

            ax.scatter(
                xs[rep_indices], ys[rep_indices],
                color="crimson",
                edgecolors="black",
                linewidths=0.8,
                s=180,
                marker="*",
                zorder=7,
                label=concept,
            )

    # Arrows
    vars_to_plot = selected_vars if selected_vars is not None else range(coeff.shape[0])
    base_scale = 10

    arrowprops = dict(
        arrowstyle="-|>",
        color="#2B2B2B",
        lw=1.5,
        mutation_scale=12,
    )

    for i in vars_to_plot:
        var_name = f"Var{i+1}" if labels is None else labels[i]
        scale = base_scale * (arrow_strength.get(var_name, 1.0) if arrow_strength else 1.0)
        ex, ey = coeff[i, ix] * scale, coeff[i, iy] * scale

        ax.annotate(
            "",
            xy=(ex, ey),
            xytext=(0, 0),
            arrowprops=arrowprops,
            zorder=4,
        )

        if show_labels:
            # Nudge label slightly beyond arrow tip
            offset = 0.05 * np.array([ex, ey])
            ax.text(
                ex + offset[0], ey + offset[1],
                var_name,
                fontsize=8.5,
                ha="center",
                va="center",
                color="#2B2B2B",
                fontweight="semibold",
                bbox=dict(
                    boxstyle="round,pad=0.2",
                    facecolor="white",
                    edgecolor="none",
                    alpha=0.75,
                ),
                zorder=5,
            )

    # Labels & title 
    ax.set_xlabel(f"PC{pc_x}", fontsize=13, labelpad=8, color="#333333")
    ax.set_ylabel(f"PC{pc_y}", fontsize=13, labelpad=8, color="#333333")
    ax.set_title(
        f"PCA Biplot — PC{pc_x} vs PC{pc_y}",
        fontsize=15,
        fontweight="bold",
        color="#1A1A1A",
        pad=14,
    )
    ax.tick_params(colors="#555555", labelsize=9)

    # Legend (groups only, centroids explained in title note) 
    group_handles = [
        mpatches.Patch(color=color_map[g], label=group_name(g), alpha=0.8)
        for g in groups
    ]
    centroid_handle = plt.Line2D(
        [0], [0],
        marker="X",
        color="w",
        markerfacecolor="#555555",
        markeredgecolor="white",
        markersize=9,
        label="Centroid",
    )
    handles = group_handles + [centroid_handle]

    if concepts is not None and highlight_concepts is not None:
        for concept in highlight_concepts:
            handles.append(
                plt.Line2D(
                    [0], [0],
                    marker="*",
                    color="w",
                    markerfacecolor="crimson",
                    markeredgecolor="black",
                    markersize=11,
                    label=concept,
                )
            )

    ax.legend(
        handles=handles,
        loc="best",
        fontsize=9,
        framealpha=0.9,
        edgecolor="#CCCCCC",
        fancybox=False,
    )

    plt.tight_layout()

    if save_path:
        fig.savefig(save_path, dpi=dpi, bbox_inches="tight", facecolor=fig.get_facecolor())

    plt.show()
    return fig, ax

Bootstrap PCA
PCA involves a sampling procedure, therefore the results can always change depending on the randomization. Therefore we employ bootstrapping to identify the interval for each component (and later also for each feature).
See Wilson Black et al. (2023) for more detail.

def bootstrap_pca(Xz, n_boot=1000):

    rng = np.random.default_rng(42)

    boot_loadings = []
    boot_eigs = []

    n = Xz.shape[0]

    for _ in range(n_boot):
        idx = rng.choice(n, n, replace=True)
        Xb = Xz[idx]
        pca_b = PCA().fit(Xb)
        boot_loadings.append(pca_b.components_.T)
        boot_eigs.append(pca_b.explained_variance_)

    boot_loadings = np.array(boot_loadings)
    boot_eigs = np.array(boot_eigs)

    # total variance per bootstrap PCA (needed to convert eigvals -> variance explained)
    boot_total_var = np.sum(boot_eigs, axis=1, keepdims=True)

    # bootstrap variance explained per PC
    boot_var_explained = boot_eigs / boot_total_var

    # mean and SD of bootstrap variance explained
    boot_var_mean = boot_var_explained.mean(axis=0)
    boot_var_sd = boot_var_explained.std(axis=0)

    # # sanity check shapes
    # print(boot_var_mean.shape, boot_var_sd.shape)

    loading_ci_low = np.percentile(boot_loadings, 5, axis=0)
    loading_ci_high = np.percentile(boot_loadings, 95, axis=0)

    eig_ci_low = np.percentile(boot_eigs, 2.5, axis=0)
    eig_ci_high = np.percentile(boot_eigs, 97.5, axis=0)

    # bind all results into a dictionary for easy access
    results = {
        "boot_loadings": boot_loadings,
        "boot_eigs": boot_eigs,
        "boot_var_mean": boot_var_mean,
        "boot_var_sd": boot_var_sd,
        "loading_ci_low": loading_ci_low,
        "loading_ci_high": loading_ci_high,
        "eig_ci_low": eig_ci_low,
        "eig_ci_high": eig_ci_high
    }

    return results

bootstrap_results_GS = bootstrap_pca(Xz_GS)



Null PCA (permutation test)
Additionally, we again perform permutation to identify the null distribution. If any component (or later feature) crosses this threshold, it cannot be considered as a realible dimension and we will not interpret them further.
See Wilson Black et al. (2023) for more detail.

def permutation_pca(Xz, n_boot=1000):

    rng = np.random.default_rng(42)

    null_loadings = []
    null_eigs = []

    for _ in range(n_boot):
        #
        Xnull = np.apply_along_axis(rng.permutation, 0, Xz)
        pca_n = PCA().fit(Xnull)
        null_loadings.append(pca_n.components_.T)
        null_eigs.append(pca_n.explained_variance_)

    null_loadings = np.array(null_loadings)
    null_eigs = np.array(null_eigs)

    null_loading_thresh = np.percentile(np.abs(null_loadings), 95, axis=0)
    null_eig_thresh = np.percentile(null_eigs, 95, axis=0)

    results = {
        "null_loadings": null_loadings,
        "null_eigs": null_eigs,
        "null_loading_thresh": null_loading_thresh,
        "null_eig_thresh": null_eig_thresh
    }

    return results

Function to plot variance
def plot_pca_variance(var_explained,
                             boot_ci_low,
                             boot_ci_high,
                             null_thresh,
                             max_pcs=20):
    """
    var_explained: array of variance explained ratios (e.g. pca.explained_variance_ratio_)
    boot_ci_low: bootstrap CI lower bound (variance ratio)
    boot_ci_high: bootstrap CI upper bound (variance ratio)
    null_thresh: null 95% threshold (variance ratio)
    """

    pcs = np.arange(1, len(var_explained) + 1)

    # optionally truncate to first N PCs (keeps plot readable)
    pcs = pcs[:max_pcs]
    var_explained = var_explained[:max_pcs]
    boot_ci_low = boot_ci_low[:max_pcs]
    boot_ci_high = boot_ci_high[:max_pcs]

    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

    # CI bars
    plt.vlines(
        pcs,
        boot_ci_low * 100,
        boot_ci_high * 100,
        colors='black',
        linewidth=1,
        alpha=0.7
    )

    # observed variance points
    plt.scatter(
        pcs,
        var_explained * 100,
        color='red',
        s=40,
        zorder=3,
        label="Sampling"
    )

    # null threshold line
    plt.plot(
    pcs,
    null_thresh[:len(pcs)] * 100,
    linestyle='--',
    color='teal',
    linewidth=2,
    label="Null"
)


    plt.xlabel("Principal Component")
    plt.ylabel("Variance Explained (%)")
    plt.title("Variance Explained by Principal Components")

    plt.xticks(pcs, [f"PC{i}" for i in pcs], rotation=90)
    plt.legend()
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

Significant variables
Now we will look into which variables significantly contribute to each component. We will identify them with the same checks as we did for the components, using bootstrapping and permutation.

def identify_sigvar(pca, bootstrap_results, permutation_results, df_clean):

    # compute index loadings
    loadings = pca.components_.T
    eigs = pca.explained_variance_

    # index loadings for original PCA
    index_loadings = (loadings ** 2) * (eigs ** 2)

    # compute bootrap index loadings
    boot_index_loadings = (bootstrap_results["boot_loadings"] ** 2) * (bootstrap_results["boot_eigs"][:, None, :] ** 2)

    # 90% CI (matches loadings_confint = 0.9)
    low_q = 5
    high_q = 95

    boot_index_ci_low = np.percentile(boot_index_loadings, low_q, axis=0)
    boot_index_ci_high = np.percentile(boot_index_loadings, high_q, axis=0)

    # compute null index loadings
    null_index_loadings = (permutation_results["null_loadings"] ** 2) * (permutation_results["null_eigs"][:, None, :] ** 2)

    null_index_ci_low = np.percentile(null_index_loadings, low_q, axis=0)
    null_index_ci_high = np.percentile(null_index_loadings, high_q, axis=0)

    sig_vars = []

    for pc in range(loadings.shape[1]):
        for feat in range(loadings.shape[0]):
            sig_vars.append({
                "PC": pc + 1,
                "feature": df_clean.columns[feat],
                "loading": loadings[feat, pc],
                "index_loading": index_loadings[feat, pc],
                "low_confint": boot_index_ci_low[feat, pc],
                "high_confint": boot_index_ci_high[feat, pc],
                "low_null": null_index_ci_low[feat, pc],
                "high_null": null_index_ci_high[feat, pc],
                "sig_loading": index_loadings[feat, pc] > null_index_ci_high[feat, pc]
            })

    df_sig_vars = pd.DataFrame(sig_vars)

    return df_sig_vars

Following Wilson Black and colleagues (2023), we also filter the features because we are dealing with a big overlap of the bootstrap intervals, which make it difficult to identify the exact order. Note however, that we are not searching for the best features per component, as we will later model the component as a whole.


Functions to plot loadings
def index_loadings_pc(pca, bootstrap_results, permutation_results, pc_idx,
                      feature_names, loadings_confint=0.9,
                      filter_boots=False, quantile_threshold=0.25):
    """Index loadings for one PC, with optional filter_boots stabilisation
    (matches nzilbb.vowels::plot_loadings). Returns (tidy_df, n_kept_iterations)."""
    half = (1 - loadings_confint) / 2
    lowq, highq = 100 * half, 100 * (1 - half)          # 5 / 95 for confint=0.9

    # observed index loadings for this PC
    obs_l = pca.components_.T[:, pc_idx]
    obs_e = pca.explained_variance_[pc_idx]
    obs_index = (obs_l ** 2) * (obs_e ** 2)

    # bootstrap index loadings: (n_boot, n_feat)
    bl = bootstrap_results["boot_loadings"][:, :, pc_idx]
    be = bootstrap_results["boot_eigs"][:, pc_idx][:, None]
    boot_index = (bl ** 2) * (be ** 2)

    kept = np.ones(boot_index.shape[0], dtype=bool)
    if filter_boots:
        winner = int(np.argmax(np.median(boot_index, axis=0)))       # highest-median variable
        thresh = np.percentile(boot_index[:, winner], 100 * quantile_threshold)
        kept = boot_index[:, winner] >= thresh                       # top 3/4 of its distribution
    bi = boot_index[kept]

    # null threshold (permuted iterations are NOT filtered, matching R)
    nl = permutation_results["null_loadings"][:, :, pc_idx]
    ne = permutation_results["null_eigs"][:, pc_idx][:, None]
    null_index = (nl ** 2) * (ne ** 2)

    df = pd.DataFrame({
        "variable": feature_names,
        "obs_index": obs_index,
        "boot_low":  np.percentile(bi, lowq,  axis=0),
        "boot_high": np.percentile(bi, highq, axis=0),
        "null_thresh": np.percentile(null_index, highq, axis=0),
        "loading_sign": np.sign(obs_l),
    })
    df["sig_loading"] = df["obs_index"] > df["null_thresh"]
    return df.sort_values("obs_index").reset_index(drop=True), int(kept.sum())


def plot_loadings_compare(pca, bootstrap_results, permutation_results, pc_idx,
                          feature_names, pc_name=None, loadings_confint=0.9,
                          quantile_threshold=0.25):
    """Side-by-side unfiltered vs filtered index-loading plot for one PC."""
    pc_name = pc_name or f"PC{pc_idx + 1}"
    df_uf, n_uf = index_loadings_pc(pca, bootstrap_results, permutation_results, pc_idx,
                                    feature_names, loadings_confint, filter_boots=False)
    df_fl, n_fl = index_loadings_pc(pca, bootstrap_results, permutation_results, pc_idx,
                                    feature_names, loadings_confint, filter_boots=True,
                                    quantile_threshold=quantile_threshold)
    order = df_uf["variable"].tolist()                     # keep both panels on same x-order
    df_fl = df_fl.set_index("variable").loc[order].reset_index()

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(18, 6), sharey=True)
    for ax, df, title, n in [(axes[0], df_uf, "Unfiltered bootstrap", n_uf),
                             (axes[1], df_fl, "Filtered bootstrap",   n_fl)]:
        x = np.arange(len(df))
        ax.vlines(x, df["boot_low"], df["boot_high"], color="red", alpha=0.6, lw=2,
                  label="Bootstrap CI")
        ax.hlines(df["null_thresh"].mean(), -1, len(df), color="turquoise",
                  ls="--", lw=2, label="Null threshold")
        for i, r in df.iterrows():
            ax.plot(i, r["obs_index"], marker=("+" if r["loading_sign"] > 0 else "_"),
                    color="black", ms=10)
        ax.set_xticks(x); ax.set_xticklabels(df["variable"], rotation=90)
        ax.set_title(f"{title} ({n} iters)"); ax.set_ylabel("Index loading"); ax.legend()
    fig.suptitle(f"Index loadings for {pc_name}: unfiltered vs filtered", fontsize=14)
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    return df_uf, df_fl

def identify_sigvar_filtered(pca, bootstrap_results, permutation_results, feature_names,
                             loadings_confint=0.9, quantile_threshold=0.25, n_pcs=None):
    n_pcs = n_pcs or pca.components_.shape[0]
    out = []
    for pc in range(n_pcs):
        df, n_kept = index_loadings_pc(pca, bootstrap_results, permutation_results, pc,
                                       feature_names, loadings_confint,
                                       filter_boots=True, quantile_threshold=quantile_threshold)
        out.append(df.assign(PC=pc + 1, kept_iterations=n_kept))
    return pd.concat(out, ignore_index=True)

def top_until_50pct(index_loadings_pc, feature_names):
    total = index_loadings_pc.sum()
    df = pd.DataFrame({
        "feature": feature_names,
        "index_loading": index_loadings_pc
    }).sort_values("index_loading", ascending=False)
    
    df["cum_frac"] = df["index_loading"].cumsum() / total
    return df[df["cum_frac"] <= 0.5]

Now we want to save the component scores, together with the feature loadings, which will be both used in the modeling script

def select_features_for_pc(pca, bootstrap_results, permutation_results, feature_names,
                           pc_idx, loadings_confint=0.9, quantile_threshold=0.25,
                           verbose=True):
    """Which variables stay in a PC for modelling, accounting for filter_boots.
    keep = significant (obs > null) AND stable after filtering (filtered boot_low > null)."""
    fn = list(feature_names)
    df_uf, _   = index_loadings_pc(pca, bootstrap_results, permutation_results, pc_idx,
                                   fn, loadings_confint, filter_boots=False)
    df_fl, n_k = index_loadings_pc(pca, bootstrap_results, permutation_results, pc_idx,
                                   fn, loadings_confint, filter_boots=True,
                                   quantile_threshold=quantile_threshold)
    # anchor = the variable the filter selects on (highest median bootstrap index loading)
    bl = bootstrap_results["boot_loadings"][:, :, pc_idx]
    be = bootstrap_results["boot_eigs"][:, pc_idx][:, None]
    boot_index = (bl ** 2) * (be ** 2)
    winner = fn[int(np.argmax(np.median(boot_index, axis=0)))]

    tbl = (df_uf.rename(columns={"boot_low": "boot_low_unfilt", "boot_high": "boot_high_unfilt"})
           .merge(df_fl.rename(columns={"boot_low": "boot_low_filt",
                                        "boot_high": "boot_high_filt"})
                        [["variable", "boot_low_filt", "boot_high_filt"]], on="variable"))
    tbl["sig_obs"]       = tbl["obs_index"]       > tbl["null_thresh"]   # exclusion rule
    tbl["stable_unfilt"] = tbl["boot_low_unfilt"] > tbl["null_thresh"]
    tbl["stable_filt"]   = tbl["boot_low_filt"]   > tbl["null_thresh"]   # survives stabilisation
    tbl["is_anchor"]     = tbl["variable"] == winner
    tbl["keep"]          = tbl["sig_obs"] & tbl["stable_filt"]
    tbl = tbl.sort_values("obs_index", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
    tbl["share"]        = tbl["obs_index"] / tbl["obs_index"].sum()
    # cumulative share of this PC's total index loading (over ALL features), largest first
    tbl["cum_frac"]     = tbl["obs_index"].cumsum() / tbl["obs_index"].sum()
    tbl["within_50pct"] = tbl["cum_frac"] <= 0.5
    keep = tbl.loc[tbl["keep"], "variable"].tolist()
    if verbose:
        print(f"PC{pc_idx+1}: filtered {n_k} iters | anchor={winner} | "
              f"sig(obs>null)={tbl['sig_obs'].sum()} | keep(sig & stable_filt)={len(keep)}")
    return tbl, keep


# Build the per-PC table for every significant PC, keep ALL significant features,
# and record CI-vs-null status before and after stabilization.
sig_pcs = np.where(sig_pc_GS)[0]                      # 0-based significant PC indices

for pc in sig_pcs:

# Prepare data

y = df_clean.iloc[:, -1].values   # Last column as target variable

# Convert categorical target to numeric if necessary

    le = LabelEncoder()
    y = le.fit_transform(y)  # Converts categorical labels into numeric labels

# Scale the data
scaler_GSG = StandardScaler()
Xz_GSG = scaler_GSG.fit_transform(X)    

# PCA transformation
pca_GSG = PCA()
x_new_GSG = pca_GSG.fit_transform(Xz_GSG)

# Get the PCA loadings (components_ is shape: [n_components, n_features])
loadings_GSG = pca_GSG.components_.T

# Number of top variables to show per PC
top_n = 10

# Get top variables per PC by absolute contribution
top_vars = set()
for i in range(2):  # PC1 and PC2 (the PCs you plot below)
    component = loadings_GSG[:, i]      # column i = all variables' loadings ON PC i
    top_indices = np.argsort(np.abs(component))[-top_n:]
    top_vars.update(top_indices)

# Convert to sorted list for consistency
selected_vars = sorted(top_vars)

# read it
df_clean = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(curfolder, 'Datasets', 'sampled_merged_sapiens_cleanforPCA_noprune.csv'))
# get rid of all columns with fine_ in the name
cols_to_drop = [col for col in df_clean.columns if col.startswith('gross_')]
df_clean = df_clean.drop(columns=cols_to_drop)


feature_names = df_clean.columns[:-1].to_list()

# Prepare data
X = df_clean.iloc[:, :-1].values  # All columns except the last as features

df_clean['groupID'] = df_clean['groupID'].astype('category')
y = df_clean.iloc[:, -1].values   # Last column as target variable

# Convert categorical target to numeric if necessary
if y.dtype == 'object' or y.dtype.name == 'category':
    le = LabelEncoder()
    y = le.fit_transform(y)  # Converts categorical labels into numeric labels

# Scale the data
scaler_GSF = StandardScaler()
Xz_GSF = scaler_GSF.fit_transform(X)    

# PCA transformation
pca_GSF = PCA()
x_new_GSF = pca_GSF.fit_transform(Xz_GSF)

# Get the PCA loadings (components_ is shape: [n_components, n_features])
loadings_GSF = pca_GSF.components_.T

# Number of top variables to show per PC
top_n = 10

# Get top variables per PC by absolute contribution
top_vars = set()
for i in range(2):  # PC1 and PC2 (the PCs you plot below)
    component = loadings_GSF[:, i]      # column i = all variables' loadings ON PC i
    top_indices = np.argsort(np.abs(component))[-top_n:]
    top_vars.update(top_indices)

# Convert to sorted list for consistency
selected_vars = sorted(top_vars)

PCA: Sign-only (drop gesturers)
This section refits the PCA on signers only (drop Gesture; keep Learner_1, Learner_2, Sign), re-standardizing features within the sign-only subset, so the leading components describe variation among signers.

Prep: signers-only subset, aligned with metadata

# fresh full feature frame (all features, LP already excluded); drop gesturers, keep row alignment
df_full = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(features, 'sampled_merged_sapiens.csv'))

# drop last column (concept)
df_full = df_full.iloc[:, :-1]

# sampled_df (metadata source) and df_full are assumed row-aligned by the pooled exports;
# verify before masking so we never misalign scores and metadata
_sd = df.reset_index(drop=True)
assert len(_sd) == len(df_full), "sampled_df and feature frame differ in length — alignment broken"

# domain-separated feature frames (groupID stays the last column in each)

# one function reproducing the pooled per-block pipeline, on the sign-only subset
def run_signonly_block(df_block, sampled_block, tag, n_boot=1000):
    feature_names = df_block.columns[:-1].to_list()
    X  = df_block.iloc[:, :-1].values

    scaler = StandardScaler()                    # RE-STANDARDIZE within the sign-only subset
    Xz     = scaler.fit_transform(X)
    pca    = PCA()
    x_new  = pca.fit_transform(Xz)

    boot = bootstrap_pca(Xz, n_boot=n_boot)
    perm = permutation_pca(Xz, n_boot=n_boot)

    var_exp  = pca.explained_variance_ratio_
    null_thr = perm["null_eig_thresh"] / np.sum(pca.explained_variance_)   # eig -> variance ratio
    sig_pc   = (var_exp > null_thr) & (var_exp > 0.05)                     # null AND >=5%, pooled rule
    print(f"[{tag}] significant PCs: {list(np.where(sig_pc)[0] + 1)}  "
          f"var={np.round(var_exp[sig_pc], 3)}")

    df_sig_vars = identify_sigvar(pca, boot, perm, df_block)   # feature order for varimax step

    sig_idx = np.where(sig_pc)[0]
    if len(sig_idx):
        # ---- scores (mirror of pca_scores_*.csv) ----
        pc_cols = [f"PC{i+1}" for i in sig_idx]
        scores  = pd.DataFrame(x_new[:, sig_idx], columns=pc_cols)
        meta = (sampled_block[['group', 'groupID', 'concept']]
                .reset_index(drop=True).rename(columns={'group': 'participant'}))
        assert len(meta) == len(scores), "row mismatch — metadata not aligned with scores!"
        out = pd.concat([scores, meta], axis=1)
        for row in out.itertuples():
            if isinstance(row.participant, str) and row.participant.startswith('IP'):
                out.loc[row.Index, 'participant'] = row.participant.split('_')[0]
        out.to_csv(os.path.join(curfolder, 'Datasets', f'pca_scores_{tag}_signonly.csv'), index=False)

        # ---- loadings (mirror of loadings_*.csv) ----
        tables = []
        for pc in sig_idx:
            tbl, _ = select_features_for_pc(pca, boot, perm, feature_names, pc_idx=pc, verbose=False)
            tables.append(tbl.assign(PC=pc + 1))
        sig_features = (pd.concat(tables, ignore_index=True)
                        .query("sig_obs")
                        .rename(columns={"stable_unfilt": "CI_above_null_before",
                                         "stable_filt":   "CI_above_null_after"})
                        [["PC", "variable", "loading_sign", "obs_index", "null_thresh",
                          "boot_low_unfilt", "boot_high_unfilt", "boot_low_filt", "boot_high_filt",
                          "CI_above_null_before", "CI_above_null_after", "is_anchor", "share", "cum_frac", "within_50pct"]]
                        .sort_values(["PC", "obs_index"], ascending=[True, False])
                        .reset_index(drop=True))
        sig_features.to_csv(os.path.join("Datasets", f"loadings_{tag}_signonly.csv"), index=False)
    else:
        print(f"[{tag}] no significant PCs — nothing exported.")

    return dict(tag=tag, scaler=scaler, pca=pca, x_new=x_new, Xz=Xz,
                boot=boot, perm=perm, sig_pc=sig_pc, df_sig_vars=df_sig_vars,
                feature_names=feature_names)

signonly = {tag: run_signonly_block(b, sampled_so, tag) for tag, b in blocks_so.items()}

def variance_table(pca, boot, sig_pc, domain, basis):
    ve  = pca.explained_variance_ratio_
    bve = boot["boot_eigs"] / boot["boot_eigs"].sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)   # per-draw ratios
    idx = np.where(sig_pc)[0]
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "basis": basis, "domain": domain, "PC": idx + 1,
        "var_exp":  ve[idx],
        "var_low":  np.percentile(bve[:, idx], 2.5,  axis=0),
        "var_high": np.percentile(bve[:, idx], 97.5, axis=0),
        "cum_var":  np.cumsum(ve)[idx],
    })

# pooled PCA (all signers + gesturers)
pooled = {
    "all":   (pca_GS,  bootstrap_results_GS,  sig_pc_GS),
    "gross": (pca_GSG, bootstrap_results_GSG, sig_pc_GSG),
    "fine":  (pca_GSF, bootstrap_results_GSF, sig_pc_GSF),
}

var_tab = pd.concat(
    # pooled: all / gross / fine
    [variance_table(p, b, s, dom, "pca") for dom, (p, b, s) in pooled.items()] +
    # sign-only: all / gross / fine
    [variance_table(signonly[dom]["pca"], signonly[dom]["boot"], signonly[dom]["sig_pc"], dom, "signonly")
     for dom in ["all", "gross", "fine"]],
    ignore_index=True,
)

var_tab.to_csv(os.path.join("Datasets", "pca_variance_explained.csv"), index=False)

title: Processing II: Motion processing
text:
Pre-Process json to csv
Besides converting json into workable csv, we also want to prevent having more people in the dataframe. Because the person of interest is expected to be the (i) largest and (ii) the most central, we will apply two filters which will help us to order the people in the frame. In the next step, we will exclude all persons except the first.


Helper functions
def unwrap(d):
    """Extracts frames, fps, video name, and prediction data from a nested dictionary structure.
    Handles three cases:
    1. Prediction block present alone
    2. Prediction block mixed with per-frame entries
    3. Dictionary of per-frame entries only
    Returns (frames, fps, video, pred) tuple."""
    fps, video = d.get("fps"), d.get("video")
    node, pred = d["frames"], None
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        cands = [v for v in node.values() if isinstance(v, dict) and "frames" in v]
        if cands:
            # cases 1 & 2: prediction block present (alone or mixed with per-frame entries)
            pred = cands[0]
            video = video or pred.get("video")
            node = pred["frames"]
        else:
            # case 3: dict of per-frame entries only
            node = [v for k, v in sorted(node.items())
                    if isinstance(v, dict) and "instances" in v]
    return node, fps, video, pred

def get_image_size(pred, video, video_dir=None, default=(1080, 1920)):
    """Returns (H, W)."""
    if pred is not None and "image_size" in pred:
        return pred["image_size"]
    if video_dir is not None:
        for ext in (".mp4", ".mov", ".avi", ".MP4", ".MOV"):
            vp = os.path.join(video_dir, video + ext)
            if os.path.exists(vp):
                cap = cv2.VideoCapture(vp)
                W = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH))
                H = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_HEIGHT))
                cap.release()
                if W and H:
                    return H, W
    print(f"  warning: no image_size for {video}, using default {default}")
    return default

def person_center(inst):
    """Calculates the center of a person's bounding box or keypoints.
    If keypoints with sufficient confidence exist, returns their mean position.
    Otherwise falls back to the center of the bounding box."""
    kp = np.array(inst["keypoints"], float)
    sc = np.array(inst["keypoint_scores"], float)
    good = sc >= CONF_THR
    if good.sum() == 0:
        x1, y1, x2, y2 = inst["bbox"]
        return np.array([(x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2])
    return kp[good].mean(axis=0)

def person_trunk_size(inst):
    """Shoulder->hip height; falls back to shoulder width if hips aren't confident."""
    kp = np.array(inst["keypoints"], float)
    sc = np.array(inst["keypoint_scores"], float)
    good = sc >= CONF_THR
    def pt(name):
        i = IDX[name]; return kp[i] if good[i] else None
    ls, rs = pt("left_shoulder"), pt("right_shoulder")
    lh, rh = pt("left_hip"), pt("right_hip")
    if ls is not None and rs is not None and lh is not None and rh is not None:
        return np.linalg.norm((lh + rh) / 2 - (ls + rs) / 2)   # trunk height
    if ls is not None and rs is not None:
        return np.linalg.norm(ls - rs)                          # fallback: shoulder width
    return 0.0

def person_score(inst, cx, cy):
    """Lower = more central AND larger (nearer). inf if no usable trunk."""
    c = person_center(inst)
    dist = np.hypot(c[0] - cx, c[1] - cy)
    trunk = person_trunk_size(inst)
    if trunk <= 0:
        return np.inf
    return dist / trunk

def order_by_center_and_trunk(instances, cx, cy):
    return sorted(instances, key=lambda i: person_score(i, cx, cy))

def json_to_wide_csv(json_path, csv_path):
    """Converts JSON prediction data to wide-format CSV.
    Processes keypoint data for multiple persons per frame, ordered by centrality and size.
    Output includes video name, frame index, timestamp, and all keypoints with confidence scores.
    Returns the maximum number of persons detected across all frames."""
    with open(json_path) as f:
        d = json.load(f)
    frames, fps, video, pred = unwrap(d)

    H, W = get_image_size(pred, video, video_dir=vidfolder)
    cx, cy = W / 2, H / 2

    n_persons = max((len(fr["instances"]) for fr in frames), default=1)
    header = ["video", "frame", "time_s"]
    for p in range(1, n_persons + 1):
        for nm in KP_NAMES:
            header += [f"p{p}_{nm}_x", f"p{p}_{nm}_y", f"p{p}_{nm}_conf"]

    with open(csv_path, "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(header)
        for fr in frames:
            idx = int(os.path.splitext(fr["image_name"])[0])
            row = {"video": video, "frame": idx, "time_s": idx / fps if fps else ""}
            insts = order_by_center_and_trunk(fr["instances"], cx, cy)
            for p, inst in enumerate(insts, 1):
                for nm, (x, y), s in zip(KP_NAMES, inst["keypoints"], inst["keypoint_scores"]):
                    row[f"p{p}_{nm}_x"] = x
                    row[f"p{p}_{nm}_y"] = y
                    row[f"p{p}_{nm}_conf"] = s
            w.writerow([row.get(c, "") for c in header])
    return n_persons

def person_xy(row, p):
    """Return (308x2 array, 308 conf) for person p from a dataframe row; NaN where missing."""
    xs = np.array([row.get(f"p{p}_{n}_x", np.nan) for n in KP_NAMES], float)
    ys = np.array([row.get(f"p{p}_{n}_y", np.nan) for n in KP_NAMES], float)
    cs = np.array([row.get(f"p{p}_{n}_conf", np.nan) for n in KP_NAMES], float)
    return np.column_stack([xs, ys]), cs

def draw(img, kpts, conf, color, thr=0.3):
    for a, b in SKELETON_EDGES:
        if conf[a] < thr or conf[b] < thr: continue
        if np.isnan(kpts[[a, b]]).any(): continue
        cv2.line(img, tuple(kpts[a].astype(int)), tuple(kpts[b].astype(int)), color, 2)
    for i in range(len(kpts)):
        if conf[i] < thr or np.isnan(kpts[i]).any(): continue
        cv2.circle(img, tuple(kpts[i].astype(int)), 4, color, -1)

text:
Further processing (on sample)
Now we will perform all planned processing steps on a single file, before continuing with full loop.

Cleaning
As part of cleaning procedure, we delete all columns that we do not need for our purposes, flip the y-axis such that up in motion corresponds to up in the image, and we interpolate the missing values whenever there is maximum 10 missing consecutive samples.

csvfiles = glob.glob(os.path.join(curfolder, 'Sapiens_Output', '*', '*_pose.csv'))
csvsample = csvfiles[400]

TOKEEP = ['nose', 'shoulder', 'elbow', 'hip', 'thumb', 'finger', 'wrist', 'neck']

# Flip the y axis to correnspond to up and down
def flip_axis(df):
    cols = [col for col in df.columns if '_y' in col]
    
    # Identify the maximum value in the first row of the Y_
    maxpoint = max(df.loc[0, cols])

    # Flip all Y_ columns across all rows
    for joint in cols:
        df.loc[:, joint] = maxpoint - df[joint] - 1
            
    return df

# Interpolate missing data
def interpolate(df):
    cols = df.columns
    cols = cols.drop(['time_s', 'frame', 'FileID'])

    # loop over the cols and interpolate missing data
    for col in cols:
        df[col] = df[col].interpolate(method='linear', x = df['time_s'], limit=10)
    return df

# Do all in one go
def clean_and_process_df(file, colstokeep):
    df = pd.read_csv(file)
    name = os.path.basename(file).split('_pose.csv')[0]

    # Get frame and time_s columns
    frames = df['frame']
    time_s = df['time_s']

    # Keep only p1_ columns
    df = df.loc[:, df.columns.str.contains('p1_')]
    
    # Keep only columns that share strings with elements in colstokeep
    df = df.loc[:, df.columns.str.contains('|'.join(colstokeep))]

    # Rename columns to remove p1_ prefix
    df.columns = df.columns.str.replace('p1_', '')

    # Get rid of columns that have '_of_' in (residuals of nose columns that we don't need)
    df = df.loc[:, ~df.columns.str.contains('_of_')]

    # Flip y axis
    df = flip_axis(df)

    # Add name as FileID
    df['FileID'] = name

    # Add time and frames in the beginning
    df['frame'] = frames
    df['time_s'] = time_s

    # Interpolate
    df = interpolate(df)

    return df

# sys.path.append(os.path.join(curfolder, 'Sapiens'))
from keypoints308 import dataset_info

_ki = dataset_info["keypoint_info"]
KP_NAMES = [_ki[i]["name"] for i in range(len(_ki))]
_name2id = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(KP_NAMES)}
SKELETON_EDGES = [(_name2id[a], _name2id[b], s["color"])
                  for s in dataset_info["skeleton_info"].values()
                  for a, b in [s["link"]]
                  if a in _name2id and b in _name2id]

CONF_THR = 0.3
COMBOS = [(9, 2), (15,2), (21, 2)]      # <-- your three (window, order) choices

def smooth_series(vals, conf, win, order):
    """Mask low-conf -> interpolate -> savgol. vals, conf are 1D arrays over frames."""
    s = pd.Series(vals, dtype=float)
    s[conf < CONF_THR] = np.nan
    s = s.interpolate(limit_direction="both")     # fill gaps so savgol can run
    if s.isna().all():
        return vals                                # nothing usable; leave as-is
    if len(s) <= win:
        return s.to_numpy()                        # too short to filter
    return scipy.signal.savgol_filter(s.to_numpy(), win, order)

def build_smoothed(df, person, win, order):
    """Return dict name -> (x_arr, y_arr) smoothed across all frames for one person."""
    out = {}
    for nm in KP_NAMES:
        cx = df.get(f"{person}_{nm}_x")
        cy = df.get(f"{person}_{nm}_y")
        cc = df.get(f"{person}_{nm}_conf")
        if cx is None:
            continue
        conf = cc.to_numpy() if cc is not None else np.ones(len(df))
        out[nm] = (smooth_series(cx.to_numpy(), conf, win, order),
                   smooth_series(cy.to_numpy(), conf, win, order))
    return out

def draw_skeleton(img, coords_by_name, fi, color=None):
    """Draw skeleton and keypoints on an image frame using smoothed coordinates.

    Args:
        img: Input image frame to draw on
        coords_by_name: Dictionary mapping keypoint names to (x,y) coordinate arrays
        fi: Frame index to use for drawing
        color: Optional override color for skeleton and keypoints (BGR format)
    """
    def pt(nm):
        if nm not in coords_by_name: return None
        x, y = coords_by_name[nm][0][fi], coords_by_name[nm][1][fi]
        return None if (np.isnan(x) or np.isnan(y)) else (int(x), int(y))
    for a, b, c in SKELETON_EDGES:
        pa, pb = pt(KP_NAMES[a]), pt(KP_NAMES[b])
        if pa and pb:
            cv2.line(img, pa, pb, (color or c[::-1]), 2)
    for nm in coords_by_name:
        p = pt(nm)
        if p: cv2.circle(img, p, 3, (color or (0, 255, 0)), -1)
    return img

def render_smoothing_qc(csv_path, video_path, out_dir, person="p1"):
    """Generate QC videos showing skeleton smoothing with different Savitzky-Golay filter parameters.

    Args:
        csv_path: Path to CSV file containing pose estimation data
        video_path: Path to original video file
        out_dir: Directory to save output videos
        person: Person identifier in the pose data (default: "p1")

    Creates one output video per (window, order) combination showing the smoothed skeleton.
    """
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    df = pd.read_csv(csv_path).sort_values("frame").reset_index(drop=True)
    name = os.path.basename(csv_path).split("_pose.csv")[0]

    # precompute smoothed coords for each combo
    smoothed = {combo: build_smoothed(df, person, *combo) for combo in COMBOS}

    cap = cv2.VideoCapture(video_path)
    fps = cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS)
    W = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH)); H = int(cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_HEIGHT))

    # one output video per combo
    writers = {combo: cv2.VideoWriter(
                   os.path.join(out_dir, f"{name}_savgol_w{combo[0]}_o{combo[1]}.mp4"),
                   cv2.VideoWriter_fourcc(*"mp4v"), fps, (W, H))
               for combo in COMBOS}

    for fi in range(len(df)):
        vframe = int(df.loc[fi, "frame"])
        cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES, vframe)
        ok, base = cap.read()
        if not ok: continue
        for combo in COMBOS:
            img = base.copy()
            draw_skeleton(img, smoothed[combo], fi, color=(0, 255, 0))
            cv2.putText(img, f"savgol win={combo[0]} order={combo[1]}", (12, 30),
                        cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.8, (0, 255, 0), 2)
            writers[combo].write(img)

    cap.release()
    for w in writers.values(): w.release()
    print("wrote", len(COMBOS), "videos to", out_dir)

# run on one file
filename = sample_proc['FileID'].iloc[0]
csv_path = os.path.join(curfolder, 'Sapiens_Output', filename, filename + '_pose.csv')
video_path = glob.glob(os.path.join(curfolder, "GTST_sampled", filename + "*.mp4"))[0]
render_smoothing_qc(csv_path, video_path, os.path.join(curfolder, "Smoothing_check"))


We decided for window 9, and order 2.

def savgol_smooth(df, window=21, order=2):
    """Apply Savitzky-Golay smoothing to specified columns in a DataFrame.

    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame containing columns to smooth
        window: Window size for the Savitzky-Golay filter (must be odd)
        order: Polynomial order for the Savitzky-Golay filter

    Returns:
        DataFrame with smoothed columns (columns ending with '_x' or '_y')
    """
    df_smoothed = df.copy()
    colstosmooth = [c for c in df_smoothed.columns if c.endswith('_x') or c.endswith('_y')]
    for col in colstosmooth:
            df_smoothed[col] = scipy.signal.savgol_filter(df[col], window, order)

    return df_smoothed

sample_smooth = savgol_smooth(sample_proc, window=9, order=2)

# plot wrist_y from sample_proc and sample_smooth

plt.plot(sample_smooth['right_wrist_y'], label = 'smooth')
plt.legend()

Normalization
Given the nature of the data, we need to perform three normalization steps (similar to Akamine, Dingemanse, and Özyürek 2026)

center all body-keypoint coordinates on mid-torso
normalize all body-keypoint coordinates by average torso length per participant (to account for varying bodies)
center all finger-keypoint coordinates on wrist
normalize all finger-keypoint coordinates by average palm length


def add_midtorso_and_center(
    df,
    l_shoulder_prefix="left_shoulder",
    r_shoulder_prefix="right_shoulder",
    l_hip_prefix="left_hip",
    r_hip_prefix="right_hip"):
    """
    Create mid-torso from shoulders and hips and center all XYZ keypoints on it.

    Returns a new DataFrame with:
      - X_midTorso, Y_midTorso, Z_midTorso added
      - All X_*, Y_*, Z_* centered on mid-torso
      - visibility_* and time unchanged
    """

    df = df.copy()

    # --- 1. Compute midpoints ---
    df["midtorso_x"] = 0.5 * (df[f"{l_shoulder_prefix}_x"] + df[f"{r_shoulder_prefix}_x"])
    df["midtorso_y"] = 0.5 * (df[f"{l_shoulder_prefix}_y"] + df[f"{r_shoulder_prefix}_y"])

    hips_mid_x = 0.5 * (df[f"{l_hip_prefix}_x"] + df[f"{r_hip_prefix}_x"])
    hips_mid_y = 0.5 * (df[f"{l_hip_prefix}_y"] + df[f"{r_hip_prefix}_y"])

    df["midtorso_x"] = 0.5 * (df["midtorso_x"] + hips_mid_x)
    df["midtorso_y"] = 0.5 * (df["midtorso_y"] + hips_mid_y)

    # --- 2. Center all XYZ columns on mid-torso ---
    x_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c.endswith("_x")]
    y_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c.endswith("_y")]

    # Get rid of columns with finger or thumb in
    x_cols = [c for c in x_cols if "finger" not in c and "thumb" not in c]
    y_cols = [c for c in y_cols if "finger" not in c and "thumb" not in c]

    for c in x_cols:
        df[c] = df[c] - df["midtorso_x"]
    for c in y_cols:
        df[c] = df[c] - df["midtorso_y"]

    return df

def center_fingers_on_wrist(df):
    """
    Center finger and thumb keypoints on their respective wrists.

    Returns a new DataFrame with:
      - Finger and thumb keypoints centered on wrists
      - All other columns unchanged
    """

    out = df.copy()
    cols = [c for c in df.columns if "finger" in c or "thumb" in c]

    right_cols = [c for c in cols if c.startswith("right_")]
    left_cols = [c for c in cols if c.startswith("left_")]

    # Get rid of conf columns and wrist
    right_cols = [c for c in right_cols if "conf" not in c]
    left_cols = [c for c in left_cols if "conf" not in c]

    # Center all on wrist
    for c in right_cols:
        axis = c.split('_')[-1]
        out[c] = df[c] - df[f"right_wrist_{axis}"]

    for c in left_cols:
        axis = c.split('_')[-1]
        out[c] = df[c] - df[f"left_wrist_{axis}"]

    return out

def size_normalize_by_trunk(df, trunk_len=None):
    """Normalize body keypoints by trunk length (distance between mid-shoulder and mid-hip).
    If trunk_len is not provided, it is computed from the data.
    Returns the trunk length used and the normalized dataframe."""

    if trunk_len is None:

        print("No trunk length provided, computing from data...")
    
        # create mid shoulder
        df["midshoulder_x"] = 0.5 * (df["left_shoulder_x"] + df["right_shoulder_x"])
        df["midshoulder_y"] = 0.5 * (df["left_shoulder_y"] + df["right_shoulder_y"])

        # create midhip
        df["midhip_x"] = 0.5 * (df["left_hip_x"] + df["right_hip_x"])
        df["midhip_y"] = 0.5 * (df["left_hip_y"] + df["right_hip_y"])

        # compute trunk length as median distance between mid-shoulder and mid-hip
        dx = df["midshoulder_x"] - df["midhip_x"]
        dy = df["midshoulder_y"] - df["midhip_y"]

        trunk_len = np.median(np.sqrt(dx**2 + dy**2))

    else:
        print(f"Using provided trunk length: {trunk_len}") 

    xy_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c.endswith(("_x", "_y"))]
    xy_cols = [c for c in xy_cols if 'thumb' not in c and 'finger' not in c]
    for c in xy_cols:
        df[c] = df[c] / trunk_len

    return trunk_len, df

def size_normalize_by_palm(df, palm_len=None):
    """Normalize hand keypoints by palm length (distance between forefinger and pinky).
    If palm_len is not provided, it is computed from the data.
    Returns the palm length used and the normalized dataframe."""

    if palm_len is None:

        scale_left = np.sqrt(
            (df["left_forefinger_third_joint_x"] - df["left_pinky_finger_third_joint_x"])**2 +
            (df["left_forefinger_third_joint_y"] - df["left_pinky_finger_third_joint_y"])**2
        )

        scale_right = np.sqrt(
            (df["right_forefinger_third_joint_x"] - df["right_pinky_finger_third_joint_x"])**2 +
            (df["right_forefinger_third_joint_y"] - df["right_pinky_finger_third_joint_y"])**2
        )

        scale = np.median(np.concatenate([scale_left, scale_right]))
    
    else:
        print(f"Using provided palm length: {palm_len}")
        scale = palm_len

    fingcols = [c for c in df.columns if (('finger' in c) or ('thumb' in c)) and ('conf' not in c)]
    for c in fingcols:
        df[c] = df[c] / scale

    return scale, df

trunk_len, sample_norm = size_normalize_by_trunk(sample_norm)
print(f"Trunk length used for normalization: {trunk_len}")

palm_len, sample_norm = size_normalize_by_palm(sample_norm)
print(f"Palm length used for normalization: {palm_len}")

Deriving
Now we will derive speed, acceleration and jerk. In between each derivation, we smooth the trajectories again to prevent amplification of noise.

PARENT_MAP = {
    "right_wrist": "right_elbow",  "right_elbow": "right_shoulder",
    "left_wrist":  "left_elbow",   "left_elbow":  "left_shoulder",
}

def _smooth(sig, win=9, poly=2):
    win = min(win, len(sig) - (1 - len(sig) % 2))      
    return scipy.signal.savgol_filter(sig, win, poly) if win > poly else sig

def process_derivs(df, sr):
    """Processes a DataFrame containing keypoint coordinates to compute speed, acceleration, and jerk.

    Args:
        df (pd.DataFrame): DataFrame containing keypoint coordinates with columns in format 'keypoint_x' and 'keypoint_y'.
        sr (float): Sampling rate of the data in Hz.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: The input DataFrame with additional columns for speed, acceleration, and jerk metrics.
    """
    df = df.reset_index(drop=True)

    bases = sorted({c[:-2] for c in df.columns if c.endswith(("_x", "_y"))})

    speed_dict = {}
    for b in bases:
        if f"{b}_x" not in df.columns or f"{b}_y" not in df.columns:
            continue
        x, y = df[f"{b}_x"].to_numpy(), df[f"{b}_y"].to_numpy()

        # absolute speed (torso-relative for gross kpts, palm-relative for fingers)
        speed = np.insert(np.sqrt(np.diff(x)**2 + np.diff(y)**2), 0, 0) * sr
        speed_dict[f"{b}_speed"] = _smooth(speed)

        # parent-relative speed: VECTOR diff first, THEN magnitude
        parent = PARENT_MAP.get(b)
        if parent and f"{parent}_x" in df.columns:
            px, py = df[f"{parent}_x"].to_numpy(), df[f"{parent}_y"].to_numpy()
            rdx = np.diff(x) - np.diff(px)          # <-- the fix: subtract as vectors
            rdy = np.diff(y) - np.diff(py)
            relspeed = np.insert(np.sqrt(rdx**2 + rdy**2), 0, 0) * sr
            speed_dict[f"{b}_relspeed"] = _smooth(relspeed)

    df = pd.concat([df, pd.DataFrame(speed_dict, index=df.index)], axis=1)

    # acceleration = d/dt of every speed/relspeed column 
    accel = {}
    for col in [c for c in df.columns if c.endswith("speed")]:
        a = np.insert(np.diff(df[col].to_numpy()), 0, 0) * sr
        accel[col.replace("speed", "acc")] = _smooth(a)
    df = pd.concat([df, pd.DataFrame(accel, index=df.index)], axis=1)

    # jerk = d/dt of every acc/relacc column
    jerk = {}
    for col in [c for c in df.columns if c.endswith("acc")]:
        j = np.insert(np.diff(df[col].to_numpy()), 0, 0) * sr
        jerk[col.replace("acc", "jerk")] = _smooth(j)
    df = pd.concat([df, pd.DataFrame(jerk, index=df.index)], axis=1)

    return df

Because our groups also differ in sampling rate, we will need a function to resample all to common frame rate of 30 fps.

def resample_to_fps(df, target_fps=30, time_col='time_s',
                    coord_suffixes=('_x', '_y', '_z')):
    """Resample all coordinate columns onto an exact uniform target_fps grid.
 
    Always resamples, also when the file is already ~target_fps: this removes
    timestamp jitter (variable frame rate) and puts every file on the same grid,
    so smoothing windows and derivatives mean the same thing everywhere.
 
    The grid is built as t0 + k / target_fps (no float accumulation), so
    np.diff(time) is exactly 1/target_fps.
 
    Returns (df_out, native_fps). native_fps is the average rate of the input,
    reported for logging only.
    """
    fid = df['FileID'].iloc[0] if 'FileID' in df.columns else None
 
    # sort by time and drop duplicate timestamps (np.interp needs increasing x)
    df = df.sort_values(time_col).drop_duplicates(subset=time_col, keep='first')
    t_old = df[time_col].to_numpy(float)
    if len(t_old) < 2 or t_old[-1] <= t_old[0]:
        raise ValueError(f"{fid}: fewer than 2 distinct timestamps")
 
    dur = t_old[-1] - t_old[0]
    native_fps = (len(t_old) - 1) / dur          # N samples = N-1 intervals
 
    n_new = int(np.floor(dur * target_fps + 1e-6)) + 1
    t_new = t_old[0] + np.arange(n_new) / target_fps
 
    coord_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c.endswith(coord_suffixes)]
    out = {time_col: t_new, 'frame': np.arange(n_new)}
    for c in coord_cols:
        y = df[c].to_numpy(float)
        m = ~np.isnan(y)
        out[c] = (np.interp(t_new, t_old[m], y[m]) if m.sum() >= 2
                  else np.full(n_new, np.nan))
 
    out_df = pd.DataFrame(out)
    if fid is not None:
        out_df['FileID'] = fid
    return out_df, native_fps

#### Parse filename ####
def parse_filename(stem):
    if stem.startswith("GtST_DGS"):
        return "NativeSigners", "SignerA_DGS"
    if stem.startswith("ViCom"):
        return "NativeSigners", "SignerB_ViCom"
    m = re.match(r"^(LP|IP)(\d+)_(\d+)_", stem)
    if m:
        prefix, pcn, phase = m.groups()
        phase_label = "before" if phase == "01" else "after"
        return f"{prefix}_{phase_label}", f"{prefix}{pcn}"
    m = re.match(r"^GP(\d+)_", stem)
    if m:
        return "Gestures", f"GP{m.group(1)}"
    return None, None

#### Cretae list of files #####
structure = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))

for f in vfiles:
    group, pcn = parse_filename(f.stem)
    if group is None:
        print(f"Skipping {f.name}: pattern not recognized")
        continue
    structure[group][pcn].append(f)

#### Make sure all groups are up to selected max number ####
rows = []

for group, participants in structure.items():
    remaining = TOTAL_PER_GROUP
    order = sorted(participants, key=lambda p: len(participants[p]))
    n_left = len(order)

    for pcn in order:
        share = remaining // n_left
        take = min(share, len(participants[pcn]))
        chosen = random.sample(participants[pcn], take)
        remaining -= take
        n_left -= 1

        for f in chosen:
            rows.append({"group": group, "pcnID": pcn,
                         "file": f.name, "path": str(f)})

sampled_files = pd.DataFrame(rows)

#### Sanity checks #####
print(sampled_files.groupby("group").size())
print()
print(sampled_files.groupby(["group", "pcnID"]).size())

TOTAL_PER_GROUP = 250
SEED = 42
random.seed(SEED)
REQUIRE_BOTH_SIGNERS = True   # concept must exist for signer A AND signer B

curfolder = os.getcwd()
MAPPING_PATH = Path(curfolder) / "signer_concept_map.csv"

#### Parse identifiers ######
def clean(c):
    return c.strip().replace("ẞ", "SS")   # trailing spaces + eszett fix

def parse_filename(stem):
    if stem.startswith("GtST_DGS"):
        return "NativeSigners", "SignerA_DGS", clean(stem.split("_")[2])
    if stem.startswith("ViCom"):
        return "NativeSigners", "SignerB_ViCom", clean(stem.split("_")[-1])
    m = re.match(r"^(LP|IP)(\d+)_(\d+)_(.+)$", stem)
    if m:
        prefix, pcn, phase, concept = m.groups()
        phase_label = "before" if phase == "01" else "after"
        return f"{prefix}_{phase_label}", f"{prefix}{pcn}", clean(concept)
    m = re.match(r"^GP(\d+)_(.+)$", stem)
    if m:
        return "Gestures", f"GP{m.group(1)}", clean(m.group(2))
    return None, None, None

#### Collect files ####
projectdata = os.path.join(curfolder, "ToTrack")
vfiles = glob.glob(os.path.join(projectdata, "*", "*.mp4"), recursive=True)
vfiles = [Path(f) for f in vfiles if 'flipped' not in os.path.basename(f).lower()]

records = []
for f in vfiles:
    group, pcn, concept = parse_filename(f.stem)
    if group is None:
        print(f"Skipping {f.name}: pattern not recognized")
        continue
    records.append((group, pcn, concept, f))

#### load English -> German mapping (blank german rows are excluded) ####
map_df = pd.read_csv(MAPPING_PATH).dropna(subset=["german"])
map_df = map_df[map_df["german"].str.strip() != ""]
en2de = dict(zip(map_df["english"].str.strip(),
                 map_df["german"].str.strip()))

signer_english = sorted({c for g, p, c, f in records if g == "NativeSigners"})
unmapped = [c for c in signer_english if c not in en2de]
if unmapped:
    print(f"Note: {len(unmapped)} signer concepts have no mapping and are excluded:")
    print(f"  {unmapped}")

#### Build structure
structure = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
for group, pcn, concept, f in records:
    if group == "NativeSigners":
        concept = en2de.get(concept)
        if concept is None:
            continue
    structure[group][concept].append((pcn, f))

### Anchor concept set on signers
signer_sets = defaultdict(set)
for c, pfs in structure["NativeSigners"].items():
    for pcn, f in pfs:
        signer_sets[pcn].add(c)

if REQUIRE_BOTH_SIGNERS:
    anchor = signer_sets["SignerA_DGS"] & signer_sets["SignerB_ViCom"]
else:
    anchor = signer_sets["SignerA_DGS"] | signer_sets["SignerB_ViCom"]
print(f"\nAnchor (signer) concepts: {len(anchor)}")

shared = set(anchor)
for g in structure:
    if g == "NativeSigners":
        continue
    before = len(shared)
    shared &= set(structure[g])
    print(f"  ∩ {g}: {before} -> {len(shared)}")
shared_concepts = sorted(shared)
print(f"Final shared concept set: {len(shared_concepts)}")

#### Choose the concept set
if len(shared_concepts) >= TOTAL_PER_GROUP:
    chosen_concepts = random.sample(shared_concepts, TOTAL_PER_GROUP)
else:
    chosen_concepts = shared_concepts   # cycle: multiple files per concept

#### Sample per group
rows = []
for group in structure:
    avail = {c: random.sample(structure[group][c], len(structure[group][c]))
             for c in chosen_concepts}
    counts = defaultdict(int)
    selected = []

    while len(selected) < TOTAL_PER_GROUP:
        progress = False
        for c in chosen_concepts:
            if len(selected) >= TOTAL_PER_GROUP:
                break
            if not avail[c]:
                continue
            best = min(avail[c], key=lambda pf: counts[pf[0]])
            avail[c].remove(best)
            pcn, f = best
            selected.append({"group": group, "pcnID": pcn, "concept": c,
                             "file": f.name, "path": str(f)})
            counts[pcn] += 1
            progress = True
        if not progress:
            break
    rows.extend(selected)

sampled_matched = pd.DataFrame(rows)

#### Sannity check ####

print("\nFiles per participant:")
print(sampled_matched.groupby(["group", "pcnID"]).size())

there is a dynamic timeout if the processing gets stalled and doesn’t progress
already processed frames are not processed again


# Function to run sapiens
def run_sapiens(command, cwd, total_frames, per_frame_timeout=600, poll_interval=5):
    """
    Run Sapiens subprocess with a dynamic timeout based on frame count.
    Watches posedir for new .json files; if none appear for per_frame_timeout
    seconds, kills the process and returns a timeout result.
    Returns (returncode, timed_out: bool).
    """
    total_timeout = total_frames * per_frame_timeout  # generous ceiling
    proc = subprocess.Popen(command, shell=True, cwd=cwd,
                            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    stdout_lines, stderr_lines = [], []

    def drain(pipe, store):
        for line in pipe:
            store.append(line)
    threading.Thread(target=drain, args=(proc.stdout, stdout_lines), daemon=True).start()
    threading.Thread(target=drain, args=(proc.stderr, stderr_lines), daemon=True).start()

    deadline = time.time() + total_timeout
    last_json_count = 0
    stall_since = time.time()

    while proc.poll() is None:
        time.sleep(poll_interval)
        # count json files written so far (progress signal)
        current_jsons = len(glob.glob(os.path.join(posedir, "*.json")))
        if current_jsons > last_json_count:
            last_json_count = current_jsons
            stall_since = time.time()  # reset stall clock on progress

        stalled = (time.time() - stall_since) > per_frame_timeout
        overdue  = time.time() > deadline

        if stalled or overdue:
            reason = "stalled (no new JSON)" if stalled else "total timeout exceeded"
            print(f"  TIMEOUT: {reason} — killing Sapiens")
            proc.kill()
            proc.wait()
            print("STDERR:\n", "".join(stderr_lines)[-3000:])
            return proc.returncode, True

    if proc.returncode != 0:
        print("STDERR:\n", "".join(stderr_lines)[-3000:])
        print("STDOUT:\n", "".join(stdout_lines)[-1000:])
    return proc.returncode, False

title: Processing I: Pose estimation using Sapiens2
text:
Loop over videos

sapiens_error = []
FRAME_TIMEOUT = 600  # 10 min per frame absolute ceiling; total timeout set per-video below

for vidf in vfiles:
    name = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(vidf))[0]

    print(f"working on {name}  ({vfiles.index(vidf)+1}/{len(vfiles)})")

    try:
        vdir    = os.path.join(OUTROOT, name)
        posedir = os.path.join(vdir, "pose_out")
        framedir = os.path.join(vdir, "_frames")
        merged  = os.path.join(vdir, f"{name}_pose.json")
        os.makedirs(posedir, exist_ok=True)
        os.makedirs(framedir, exist_ok=True)

        if os.path.isfile(merged):
            print("  skipping (already merged)")
            continue

        # extract frames (skip already-extracted ones)
        cap = cv2.VideoCapture(vidf)
        fps = cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS)
        f = 0
        while True:
            ok, frame = cap.read()
            if not ok: break
            fpath = os.path.join(framedir, f"{f:06d}.png")
            if not os.path.isfile(fpath):  # don't re-extract if resuming
                cv2.imwrite(fpath, frame)
            f += 1
        cap.release()
        total_frames = f
        print(f"  {total_frames} frames @ {fps:.2f} fps")

        # figure out which frames still need processing
        # a frame is done if its .json exists in posedir
        all_frame_names  = [f"{i:06d}.png" for i in range(total_frames)]
        done_jsons       = {os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(j))[0]
                            for j in glob.glob(os.path.join(posedir, "*.json"))}
        pending          = [fn for fn in all_frame_names
                            if os.path.splitext(fn)[0] not in done_jsons]
        print(f"  {len(done_jsons)} frames already done, {len(pending)} pending")

        MAX_RETRIES = 3
        attempt = 0
        
        while pending and attempt < MAX_RETRIES:
            attempt += 1
            print(f"  attempt {attempt}: running Sapiens on {len(pending)} frames")

            # write a text file listing only the pending frames
            pending_list_path = os.path.join(vdir, "_pending.txt")
            with open(pending_list_path, "w") as fh:
                for fn in pending:
                    fh.write(os.path.join(framedir, fn) + "\n")

            command = (f'"{PYTHON}" tools/vis/vis_pose.py '
                       f'"{DETECTOR}" "{CONFIG}" "{CHECKPOINT}" '
                       f'--input "{pending_list_path}" --output "{posedir}" '
                       f'--radius 6 --kpt-thr 0.3 --thickness 4 --bbox-thr 0.9')

            rc, timed_out = run_sapiens(command, cwd=POSE_DIR,
                                        total_frames=len(pending),
                                        per_frame_timeout=600)

            # recompute pending after this attempt
            done_jsons = {os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(j))[0]
                          for j in glob.glob(os.path.join(posedir, "*.json"))}
            pending    = [fn for fn in all_frame_names
                          if os.path.splitext(fn)[0] not in done_jsons]

            if not pending:
                print("  all frames processed")
                break
            elif timed_out:
                print(f"  timed out, {len(pending)} frames still pending — retrying")
            else:
                print(f"  process exited (rc={rc}), {len(pending)} frames still pending — retrying")

        if pending:
            msg = f"{len(pending)} frames never completed after {MAX_RETRIES} attempts"
            print(f"  WARNING: {msg} — skipping to next video")
            sapiens_error.append(f"File {name}: {msg}")
            continue

        # stitch overlay video
        overlays = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(posedir, "*.jpg")) +
                          glob.glob(os.path.join(posedir, "*.png")))
        if overlays:
            h, w = cv2.imread(overlays[0]).shape[:2]
            vw = cv2.VideoWriter(os.path.join(vdir, f"{name}_pose.mp4"),
                                 cv2.VideoWriter_fourcc(*"mp4v"), fps, (w, h))
            for p in overlays:
                vw.write(cv2.imread(p))
            vw.release()
        else:
            print("  WARNING: no overlay images found in", posedir)

        # merge per-frame JSONs (exclude the summary _predictions.json if present)
        summary_name = next(
            (os.path.basename(j) for j in glob.glob(os.path.join(posedir, "*.json"))
             if "_predictions" in os.path.basename(j)), None)
        jfiles = sorted(j for j in glob.glob(os.path.join(posedir, "*.json"))
                        if os.path.basename(j) != summary_name)
        combined = {"video": name, "fps": fps, "n_frames": len(jfiles), "frames": {}}
        for jf in jfiles:
            idx = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(jf))[0]
            with open(jf) as fh:
                combined["frames"][idx] = json.load(fh)
        with open(merged, "w") as fh:
            json.dump(combined, fh)
        print(f"  merged {len(jfiles)} json -> {name}_pose.json")

        # clean up scratch
        shutil.rmtree(posedir)
        shutil.rmtree(framedir)
        os.remove(pending_list_path)
        print("  cleaned scratch")

    except Exception as e:
        print("  ERROR:", e)
        sapiens_error.append(f"File {name} has error: {e}")
        continue

1 Gross / arm kinematics
These describe the movement dimension: magnitude, smoothness, rhythmicity, spatial extent, coordination, and (via the relative-speed columns) proximal-distal ratio.

Bounding box of movement volume (2D)

# Bounding-box movement volume (spatial extent of a keypoint) 
def get_bbmv(df, side, joint):
    """Area of the x-y bounding box swept by one keypoint = how much space it covers."""
    xc, yc = kp(side, joint) + "_x", kp(side, joint) + "_y"
    if xc not in df.columns or yc not in df.columns:
        return np.nan
    return (df[xc].max() - df[xc].min()) * (df[yc].max() - df[yc].min())

Intermittency (dimensionless jerk)
Calculation taken from Pouw et al. (2021).

# Intermittency / dimensionless jerk (smoothness; higher = less smooth)  
def get_intermittency(jerk_values, speed_values):
    """Calculate intermittency (dimensionless jerk) from jerk and speed values.

    Args:
        jerk_values: Array-like of jerk values (acceleration derivative)
        speed_values: Array-like of speed values (velocity magnitude)

    Returns:
        float: Intermittency value (log of sum of squared jerk multiplied by
               (n^3 / max(speed^2)), or NaN if all speeds are zero)
    """
    jerk = np.asarray(jerk_values); speed = np.asarray(speed_values)
    if np.all(speed == 0):
        return np.nan
    return np.log(np.sum(jerk ** 2) * (len(speed) ** 3 / np.max(speed ** 2)))

# SPARC — spectral arc length smoothness  
# More robust smoothness measure than dimensionless jerk (less noise/duration sensitive).
# More negative = less smooth. Keep alongside intermittency; they disagree usefully.
def get_sparc(speed, fs, fc=10.0, amp_th=0.05):
    """Compute SPARC (Spectral Arc Length Smoothness) metric for motion smoothness.
    Args:
        speed: Array-like of speed values (units: arbitrary)
        fs: Sampling frequency (Hz)
        fc: Cutoff frequency for frequency domain analysis (Hz)
        amp_th: Amplitude threshold for frequency components to include
    Returns:
        SPARC score (more negative = less smooth)
    """
    speed = np.asarray(speed, float)
    if len(speed) < 8 or np.all(speed == 0):
        return np.nan
    N = int(2 ** np.ceil(np.log2(len(speed) * 4)))     # zero-pad for resolution
    Mf = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(speed, N))
    Mf = Mf / (Mf.max() + 1e-12)
    freq = np.fft.rfftfreq(N, d=1.0 / fs)
    keep = freq <= fc
    f, M = freq[keep], Mf[keep]
    inrange = M >= amp_th                                # adaptive cutoff
    if inrange.sum() < 2:
        return np.nan
    f, M = f[inrange], M[inrange]
    df_ = np.diff(f) / (f[-1] - f[0] + 1e-12)
    return -np.sum(np.sqrt(df_ ** 2 + np.diff(M) ** 2))

# Peaks / submovements   
def compute_peaks(df, col, fs, time_col=TIME_COL):
    """Compute peak characteristics from a signal column in a DataFrame.

    Args:
        df: DataFrame containing the signal data
        col: Name of the column containing the signal
        fs: Sampling frequency of the signal
        time_col: Name of the column containing time values (default: 'time_s')

    Returns:
        Dictionary containing:
        - peak_mean: Mean of peak values
        - peak_std: Standard deviation of peak values
        - peak_n: Number of peaks detected
        - peak_rate: Peak rate (peaks per second)
        - mod_depth: Modulation depth (mean peak - mean trough)
    """
    if col not in df.columns:
        return dict(peak_mean=np.nan, peak_std=np.nan, peak_n=np.nan,
                    peak_rate=np.nan, mod_depth=np.nan)
    scale = median_abs_deviation(df[col].dropna(), scale="normal")
    prominence = scale * 0.6
    distance = int((0.1 if "acc" in col else 0.2) * fs)
    sig = np.abs(df[col].values) if "acc" in col else df[col].values
    peaks, _ = find_peaks(sig, distance=max(distance, 1), prominence=prominence)
    vals = df[col].iloc[peaks]
    duration = df[time_col].iloc[-1] - df[time_col].iloc[0]

    # peak_rate (length-normalized)
    peak_rate = len(peaks) / duration if duration > 0 else np.nan

    # modulation depth = mean(peak) - mean(trough between peaks).
    # Shallow troughs = blended/co-articulated submovements; deep = segmented.
    mod_depth = np.nan
    if len(peaks) >= 2:
        troughs = [sig[peaks[i]:peaks[i+1]].min() for i in range(len(peaks) - 1)]
        mod_depth = float(np.mean(sig[peaks]) - np.mean(troughs))

    return dict(peak_mean=float(vals.mean()) if len(vals) else np.nan,
                peak_std=float(vals.std()) if len(vals) else np.nan,
                peak_n=len(peaks), peak_rate=peak_rate, mod_depth=mod_depth)
